blocks.body_md:
JVTO publishes its rules, policies, and commitments before you pay anything. This is a deliberate choice. Guests who understand the terms before booking have better trips. Guests who discover cancellation policies at checkout do not.

This page covers what we expect of ourselves and what we ask of guests who book with us.

---

Three customer-facing policy documents are published openly at /policy:

- **Booking, Payment & Cancellation Policy** (/policy/booking-payment-cancellation) — how bookings are confirmed, deposit and balance payment timelines, the 48-hour cancellation cut-off, force-majeure procedures, and the Package Credit system. No verbal promises. The Official E-Voucher / Invoice PDF is the binding document.

- **Inclusions & Exclusions Policy** (/policy/inclusions-exclusions) — written list of what is covered in the price and what is not. The write-it-to-bind-it rule: if it is not on the voucher, it is not included. This policy is what makes the "no surprise costs" claim verifiable.

- **Privacy & Data Protection Policy** (/policy/privacy) — what data we collect (contact and booking details, participant details, safety and logistics information), how it is used, and who it is shared with. Payment cards and QRIS are processed through a PCI DSS-compliant gateway (Xendit). JVTO does not store full card numbers, CVVs, or banking credentials.

The policy hierarchy: the E-Voucher takes precedence, then the Booking Policy, then the Inclusions Policy, then the Privacy Policy, then the Travel Guide. Written documents, in order, not verbal agreements.

---

At Kawah Ijen, the trail from Paltuding to the crater rim is a shared working path. Local miners carry 70–90 kg loads of sulfur blocks from the crater floor — daily, at the same hours tourists are climbing.

JVTO guides brief every Ijen-route group on this before departure:

- **Do not block the path.** Miners are working, not trekking. Move to the side when a load-carrier approaches.
- **Do not photograph a miner without their consent.** Ask first. If they say no, respect that.

This briefing is standard, not optional. The Ijen experience includes the mining operation as a human reality of the site — not a photographic attraction.

---

JVTO recruits guides and drivers from local Bondowoso and Banyuwangi communities. The roster is not sourced from freelance marketplaces or external agencies.

JVTO is publicly listed in the INDECON (Indonesian Ecotourism Network) spotlight network. The listing is verifiable at https://www.indecon.id/spotlight-networks/java-volcano-tour-operator.

11 field crew members appear in the current roster — all with names, photos, and languages listed on the team roster page.

---

From the customer-facing policies and operational standards documented in the wiki:

- We do not collect full card numbers, CVV codes, OTP codes, or online banking passwords via chat or email. Payment is through our secure, PCI DSS-compliant gateway, Xendit.
- We do not make verbal promises that override the written voucher. If it is not on the E-Voucher, it is not included.
- We do not source crew from freelance marketplaces. Every guide and driver is a named, registered team member.
- We do not guarantee natural phenomena. Blue Fire is a natural phenomenon subject to weather and gas activity. We plan around the viewing window — we do not promise outcomes that depend on volcanic gas conditions.
- We do not operate shared groups. Every tour is private to your booking.

---

items.question: What partnerships does JVTO hold?
items.answer: JVTO is a registered ISIC provider (student identity card programme), an HPWKI member (Ijen crater operator association), and publicly listed in the INDECON ecotourism network. Details and proof links are on this page.

items.question: Is health screening on Ijen mandatory?
items.answer: Yes. Health screening is mandatory and non-negotiable for Ijen night hike routes. The system checks SpO2, blood pressure, resting heart rate, and respiratory history. No valid health certificate means no access to the crater zone.

items.question: What is the cancellation policy in brief?
items.answer: Cancelling the complete booking 48+ hours before Day 1 converts it to 100% Lifetime Package Credit — it never expires, is transferable once, and is not exchangeable for cash. Cancelling the complete booking within 48 hours of Day 1 forfeits it. The policy has explicit exceptions: if one or more travellers cancel while the tour continues, tiered cash refunds apply (100% at 48+ hours, 50% within 48 hours, 0% after Day 1), and verified destination force majeure allows a choice of Package Credit or a cash refund less non-recoverable vendor costs. Full policy: /policy/booking-payment-cancellation.

items.question: Does JVTO mix strangers into one vehicle?
items.answer: No. JVTO runs private tours only. Your vehicle and crew are allocated exclusively for your booking.

items.question: What does JVTO's ISIC provider listing mean for students?
items.answer: JVTO offers student-focused pricing on selected tours for verified ISIC cardholders. Details and eligibility are at /isic/student-package.
